newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up sharply on breach.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up sharply on breach.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index jumped 3.58 percent on Wednesday on enthusiasm sparked by the breach of the key 63-point resistance level on Wednesday, brokers said.
The B index rose 2.260 points to 65.427 points, on volume of 23.4 million shares worth $10.8 million, against $8.6 million on Wednesday.
Brokers said follow-up buying was encouraged by the breakthrough, and the index was likely to rise further to test the 68-point resistance level in the short term.

"Most investors were also boosted by expectations of positive news from an ongoing meeting in Nanjing about B shares and H shares," one broker said. "They believe Beijing wants to develop the B share market."
A second broker said the index would rise further in the short term to target the next 68-point resistance level.
Of 43 B shares, 41 traded, with 38 up, two flat and one down.
Hua Xin Cement was the star on institutional buying, with the day's heaviest volume of 2.6 million shares, soaring $0.022 or 8.46 percent to $0.282.
Property developer Shanghai Jinqiao followed, rising $0.038 or 8.26 percent to $0.498 after 480,300 shares traded.
Shanghai Tyre, the recent market leader, was the third biggest winner on institutional buying, mostly on talk that its results would show an improvement, brokers said.
It jumped $0.036 or 7.69 percent to $0.504 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai's A share market consolidated up, following the rises of the past few days, brokers said.

The A index edged up 2.569 points or 0.26 percent to 986.647 points, on volume of 352.4 million shares worth 3.5 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 1.369 points or 0.05 percent to 2553.549 points.
Xiamen Titan was the star on improved results expectations, jumping 0.42 yuan or 7.32 percent to 6.15 yuan on volume of 1.2 million shares.
